title: A Data-Driven Closed-Loop Control Approach to Drive Neural State Transitions for Mechanistic Insight.
domain: Resting-state and mood-induction fMRI; computational psychiatry
dataset_or_cohort: Remitted major depressive disorder (rMDD) and healthy-control fMRI cohort collected in Heidelberg
sample_scale: 60 participants: 30 rMDD and 30 healthy controls; 320 time points per participant across rest and sad-mood conditions
split_strategy: Within-series split: first 120 points per condition for model training and final 40 for testing; five initialized models selected using lowest test loss
observation_process: Two 4.5-minute fMRI sessions; TR 1.5 s; 11 bilateral regions represented by three principal components each (66-dimensional observations)
missingness: No explicit missing-data model reported; preprocessing and included time series were complete for the modeled segments
censoring_or_competing_events: NA: fixed experimental scans; no clinical event censoring, discharge, death, or competing-risk process
state: Latent nonlinear neural state reconstructed by a shallow piecewise-linear recurrent neural network from 66 regional principal-component signals
observation_decoder: Linear decoder maps latent state to regional fMRI observations; target affective states represented by Gaussian-mixture distributions
action: Additive, state-dependent control input, including controls restricted to individual brain regions
action_provenance: Simulated model-based control; not an administered human intervention
transition_mechanism: Shallow piecewise-linear recurrent neural network learned separately for group/condition dynamics, coupled to an optimized state-feedback controller
maximum_horizon: Control trajectories evaluated for 80 model steps; DSR train/test segments span 120/40 observed points per condition
rollout_regime: Free-running controlled model simulation toward target distributions; no real closed-loop human experiment
capability_claim: Planning: optimized feedback controls are selected from learned dynamics to move between resting and sad-mood state distributions
baselines: Uncontrolled dynamics and region-restricted control solutions; rMDD versus healthy-control models; no separate action-agnostic learned baseline beyond zero control
state_fidelity_metrics: Power-spectrum Hellinger distance (reported mean 0.22 ± 0.04), functional-connectivity cross-correlations, negative log likelihood, and target-distribution proximity
transition_metrics: Controlled trajectory convergence, target likelihood/proximity, and control energy; Lyapunov exponent reported for reconstructed dynamics (0.10 ± 0.02)
rollout_stability: Sensitivity across control horizon/regularization and target convergence is shown; no explicit physiological-constraint or long-horizon drift-rate audit
action_sensitivity: Zero-control comparison and 11 region-specific control analyses; no empirical delivered-dose or randomized action perturbation
calibration_and_uncertainty: Model/trajectory variability across five initializations is represented, but no reliability, ECE, calibration slope, or interval-coverage calibration is reported
external_validation: No frozen external, temporal, institutional, device, or population validation
decision_utility: Offline control energy and target-state reachability provide mechanistic utility; no clinician or patient decision outcome
safety_evaluation: No explicit clinical hazard, adverse-state severity, override, recovery, or deployment monitoring test
statistical_analysis: Group comparisons and associations are reported with inferential statistics; exact multiplicity coverage is only as documented in the article methods/results
causal_language: Uses mechanistic and optimal-control language for simulated transitions, not an identified clinical treatment-effect claim
estimand: NA: simulated individual/group model trajectory under an optimized controller; no population treatment-effect estimand
positivity_and_overlap: NA: simulated controls are not justified by treatment-support/overlap analysis
counterfactual_validation: Domain constraints and target-state convergence within a learned model only; no randomized or quasi-experimental counterfactual validation
weights_access: Unclear: trained model weights were not confirmed as a separately reusable artifact
data_access: Fully preprocessed study data are reported in the public repository; raw-data access was not established
preprocessing_reproducibility: Public code and preprocessed arrays support substantial reproduction; scanner preprocessing from raw data is only partially reproducible from inspected materials
randomness: Five Xavier-initialized models are trained; model-selection procedure and reported variation are described
evidence_anchors: Methods sections 'Data', 'Dynamical system reconstruction', and 'Control framework'; Results figures on reconstruction, regional controllability, control energy, and target proximity; Data Availability points to humml-lab/fmri-control
appraisal_strengths: Direct neural-state and transition evaluation, genuinely free-running control trajectories, regional action sensitivity, and public code/preprocessed data
appraisal_limitations: Small single-site cohort; final test segment participates in model selection; no external validation, formal calibration, real intervention, causal identification, or safety evaluation
source_status: Primary peer-reviewed full text inspected through Europe PMC full-text XML; repository availability checked independently

title: A digital twin for hospital antimicrobial resistance forecasting and constrained intervention optimisation
domain: Hospital epidemiology and antimicrobial resistance digital twin
dataset_or_cohort: Synthetic medium-hospital agent/contact-network simulator under canonical and shifted epidemiological/surveillance regimes
sample_scale: 10 wards, 200 patients, and 300 staff; canonical 60-day trajectories plus 360-day shifted experiments with 12 replicates per shift family
institution_count: NA: fully synthetic hospital rather than observed institutions
split_strategy: Disjoint simulation seeds for train/test; trajectory-level train/validation/test partitions for causal/action experiments; canonical-trained models are also tested zero-shot under shifts
observation_process: Daily evolving patient-staff contact graph; full latent-state setting and partially observed surveillance setting with positive/knownness channels
missingness: Partial observation is explicitly generated through delayed, less-frequent, and incomplete surveillance; incident channels are masked according to the observation regime
censoring_or_competing_events: NA: simulated fixed trajectories; importation and transmission are modeled processes rather than censoring events
state: Node/contact states encoding patient, staff, colonization/resistance, antibiotic, admission/importation, and surveillance information
observation_decoder: Forecasts resistance-spread driver and future burden; intervention branch produces policy-specific future burden/ranking
action: Five-policy library: baseline containment plus four screening/isolation variants
action_provenance: Defined simulated hospital policies applied to branched common starting states
transition_mechanism: Temporal GraphSAGE representation plus transformer forecasting; intervention selection also uses constrained mathematical programming
maximum_horizon: Input window T=7 days and forecast horizon H=7 days for primary tasks; simulator trajectories extend to 60 or 360 days
rollout_regime: Learned fixed-horizon forecasts from branched simulator states; policy evaluation uses shared past and shared deterministic noise streams rather than recursive learned rollouts
capability_claim: Planning: policy-conditioned future forecasts support constrained intervention choice and within-state action ranking
baselines: Baseline containment policy, alternative screening/isolation policies, simple predictive baselines, model ablations, full-state versus partial-state models, and canonical versus shifted training
state_fidelity_metrics: AUROC/ranking performance for endogenous-versus-importation mechanism and burden/ranking outcomes across observation regimes
transition_metrics: Seven-day forecast performance and policy-specific burden contrast; shifted-regime and zero-shot transfer results
rollout_stability: Distribution-shift and surveillance-delay/frequency stress tests; no recursive learned-model drift curve
action_sensitivity: Policy branching from common states, baseline-policy comparison, and multiple screening/isolation interventions under a shock-and-superspreader regime
calibration_and_uncertainty: Threshold fragility is discussed and probability scores are evaluated, but no formal reliability/ECE/slope or interval-coverage calibration is reported
external_validation: Synthetic zero-shot evaluation across epidemiological and surveillance shifts; not external real-hospital validation
decision_utility: Within-state action ranking and constrained policy selection against baseline containment protocols
safety_evaluation: Constraints are built into optimization and worsening policies can be detected; no real clinical hazard severity, human override, or incident-response evaluation
statistical_analysis: Multiple simulation replicates and comparisons across shift families are reported; uncertainty derives from repeated synthetic runs rather than formal predictive intervals
causal_language: Uses digital-twin, intervention-conditioned, causal-trajectory, and policy-optimization language within a fully specified simulator
estimand: Seven-day burden contrast ΔB7(a)=B7(baseline)-B7(a), with burden combining transmission and imported resistant cases
confounding_strategy: Synthetic design controls data generation; policy branches share the same history and deterministic noise streams
positivity_and_overlap: Policy library is predefined and fully executable in the simulator; real-world treatment positivity is NA
counterfactual_validation: Common-state/common-noise simulator branching validates action ranking internally; no real randomized, quasi-experimental, or target-trial validation
code_access: Public repositories reported for predictive and causal components: harrytr/dt_amr_predictive and harrytr/dt_amr_causal
weights_access: Unclear: reusable trained weights were not confirmed
data_access: Synthetic data can be regenerated through the public implementation; no real patient data are used
preprocessing_reproducibility: Code, simulator, configurations, and seed-based generation provide a reproducible synthetic pipeline
randomness: Disjoint seeds and 12 replicates per shift family are reported
evidence_anchors: Preprint Methods on synthetic hospital, T=7/H=7 graph-transformer task, partial observation, and constrained optimization; Results on surveillance perturbations, distribution shift, and intervention-conditioned branching; equations defining ΔB7(a)
appraisal_strengths: Explicit observation-process stress tests, common-noise policy comparisons, action ranking, constraints, and public generative code
appraisal_limitations: Preprint-only evidence; entirely synthetic; learned forecasts are fixed-horizon rather than demonstrated free-running world-model rollouts; no formal calibration or real external validation
source_status: Primary medRxiv PDF version 1 inspected; public code repositories identified from the preprint

split_strategy: Repository provides explicit train/test handling for Schiebinger and repeated synthetic experiments; full paper's complete split protocol NI

observation_decoder: Generates reconstructed mRNA/protein trajectories, velocity fields, and synthetic single-cell expression snapshots

title: DITTO: A Visual Digital Twin for Interventions and Temporal Treatment Outcomes in Head and Neck Cancer.

domain: Head-and-neck oncology treatment decision support and visual analytics

split_strategy: Patient-level development/evaluation split reported in Appendix A.2 (389/147); propensity-matched local comparisons are built within evaluation analyses
observation_process: Longitudinal but stage-structured oncology records covering induction chemotherapy, concurrent chemotherapy, neck dissection, disease outcomes, survival, and toxicities
missingness: Missing-variable handling is described in model/data preparation but no dedicated missingness-model validation is reported

state: Patient features plus evolving treatment/outcome state across three clinical decision stages
observation_decoder: Stage-specific treatment response, survival, locoregional control, feeding-tube dependence, and toxicity-risk outputs through the visual interface
action: Induction chemotherapy, concurrent chemotherapy, and neck dissection choices
action_provenance: Historical clinician-delivered treatments in training data; alternative treatment sequences are simulated by the digital twin
transition_mechanism: Sequential deep-reinforcement-learning/digital-twin transition components plus downstream survival, control, and toxicity models
maximum_horizon: Outcomes displayed at 12, 24, 36, and 48 months; survival/control curves extend to 5 years
rollout_regime: Sequential digital-twin branching over treatment stages with downstream outcome prediction; not a continuously recursive physiologic rollout

transition_metrics: Stage-specific and temporal outcome evaluation at 12/24/36/48 months and up to 5 years; transition fidelity itself is only indirectly evaluated through endpoints
rollout_stability: No explicit free-running drift, joint-state coherence, constraint-violation, or long-horizon stability audit
action_sensitivity: Alternative treatment sequences are displayed; propensity-matched treated/untreated comparisons use at least 5 matches within a caliper, but no action-shuffle/removal experiment is reported

decision_utility: Formative work with 11 physicians and two qualitative case studies (one involving an HNC clinician and data scientist); no prospective clinical decision trial

statistical_analysis: Quantitative predictive analyses and propensity-matched comparisons are reported; the accepted manuscript does not establish randomized causal inference
causal_language: Uses digital-twin, intervention, and treatment-outcome language, while explicitly acknowledging observational confounding limitations

title: Digital twin brain simulator for real-time consciousness monitoring and virtual intervention using primate electrocorticogram data
domain: Primate ECoG, consciousness-state monitoring, and virtual anesthesia intervention
dataset_or_cohort: Neurotycho macaque ECoG recordings in awake and anesthetized conditions
sample_scale: 4 macaques; 72 two-second sequences (144,000 modeled time steps reported) from 3 animals for core training, with the fourth serving as held-out subject in four-fold analyses
institution_count: Public Neurotycho multi-animal dataset; recording institution count not used as an evaluation split
split_strategy: Four-fold leave-one-animal-out evaluation; model is trained on three animals and evaluated/assimilated on the held-out animal
observation_process: 1 kHz ECoG from 20 channels spanning 10 regions; awake and anesthetized sequences; online assimilation uses rolling observations
missingness: Outlier samples are excluded (reported 1.4% anesthesia and 8.6% awake); no generative missingness mechanism is evaluated
censoring_or_competing_events: NA: fixed ECoG sequences; no discharge, death, or clinical competing-risk endpoint
state: Hierarchical latent state with local z1, network z2, and global z3 components intended to capture brain state and individuality
observation_decoder: Variational recurrent decoder simulates multichannel ECoG signals and latent-state trajectories
action: Virtual latent intervention intended to mimic anesthetic/drug-induced brain-state change
action_provenance: Simulated intervention in the learned model; no administered treatment randomized by the study model
transition_mechanism: Hierarchical variational Bayesian recurrent neural network with online data assimilation and latent-state updates
maximum_horizon: Primary next-step simulation plus supplementary rollouts from 1 to 100 steps; virtual intervention is simulated for 2,000 steps
rollout_regime: Free-running multistep simulation and repeated online data-assimilation cycles (rolling 500 observations with 100 update steps)
capability_claim: Action-conditioned: virtual intervention modifies latent dynamics; real-time simulation/monitoring is also claimed
baselines: Non-assimilated/model variants and held-out-animal comparisons; awake versus anesthetized conditions
state_fidelity_metrics: ECoG prediction error, power spectra, functional connectivity, latent clustering, and awake/anesthesia discriminator performance
transition_metrics: One-step prediction and supplementary 1-100-step error; held-out-subject adaptation/assimilation analyses
rollout_stability: Prediction error rises gradually across 1-100 steps; no explicit physical constraint-violation metric
action_sensitivity: Virtual intervention versus non-intervened latent trajectory and dose/state manipulations are shown in model space
calibration_and_uncertainty: Variational posterior and repeated simulations represent uncertainty, but no reliability, ECE, calibration slope, or interval-coverage calibration is reported
external_validation: Frozen leave-one-animal-out initial testing followed by assimilation/adaptation on the held-out animal; this is strong population transfer but not wholly frozen after adaptation
decision_utility: Offline consciousness-state discrimination, real-time signal simulation, and virtual intervention; no clinical workflow trial
safety_evaluation: No explicit hazard severity, harmful intervention, override, recovery, or deployment monitoring test
statistical_analysis: Cross-validation, condition comparisons, and reported inferential analyses support results; exact repeated-rollout uncertainty is limited
causal_language: Uses virtual drug administration/intervention and functional-network language, not an identified biological treatment effect
estimand: NA: model-space trajectory under virtual latent perturbation; no population clinical effect estimand
positivity_and_overlap: NA: virtual latent interventions are not tied to empirical treatment support
counterfactual_validation: Held-out-animal signal/latent behavior and biological network plausibility only; no real interventional counterfactual validation
code_access: No public code repository identified in the paper
data_access: Underlying Neurotycho ECoG data are publicly accessible
preprocessing_reproducibility: Architecture and preprocessing are described; absence of code/weights limits reproducibility
randomness: Four-fold animal splits and stochastic variational simulations are reported; exact global seed protocol is unclear
evidence_anchors: Methods 'ECoG data', hierarchical V-RNN, data assimilation, and virtual intervention; Results figures on held-out prediction, latent self-organization, spectra/connectivity, 1-100-step errors, and 2,000-step virtual intervention; Data Availability cites Neurotycho
appraisal_strengths: Leave-one-animal evaluation, explicit hierarchical states, free-running horizon analysis, online assimilation, and virtual intervention sensitivity
appraisal_limitations: Only four animals; adapted external-subject evaluation; intervention remains latent/model-based; no formal calibration, causal validation, safety testing, code, or weights
source_status: Primary peer-reviewed full text inspected through PMC XML; public data statement checked

decision_utility: High-fidelity neural simulation and downstream auditory-representation use; no clinical or control decision evaluation

statistical_analysis: Bootstrap with 1,000 replicates is reported for uncertainty/comparisons; multiple model and animal analyses are provided

estimand: NA: conditional neural-response distribution under supplied sound
positivity_and_overlap: NA: sound space is evaluated through broad held-out stimuli rather than treatment overlap
counterfactual_validation: NA: no counterfactual clinical claim; held-out stimuli and known neurophysiology provide predictive validation
code_access: Public official ICNet repository with implementation, configuration, and example assets
weights_access: Public model_weights.hdf5 is present in the official repository

title: Optimized glycemic control of type 2 diabetes with reinforcement learning: a proof-of-concept trial.
domain: Inpatient type 2 diabetes insulin decision support
dataset_or_cohort: Multicenter longitudinal inpatient EHR cohorts plus prospective clinical deployment and registered proof-of-concept trial NCT05409391
sample_scale: 12,981 inpatients and 119,941 patient-days in retrospective development/validation; physician evaluations include 40 internal and 45 external cases; prospective deployment includes 20 patients; single-arm trial includes 16 patients
institution_count: At least 3 named hospitals across development/external validation and prospective study settings
split_strategy: Patient-level development and validation partitions; frozen external-hospital testing; later prospective deployment and single-arm trial
observation_process: EHR organized into seven clinical time periods per day, including glucose, insulin, medications, laboratory/clinical context, and text-derived information
missingness: Missing clinical variables are handled in preprocessing/model inputs; no dedicated missing-not-at-random validation was identified
censoring_or_competing_events: Discharge limits inpatient trajectories; trial follow-up is short; no competing-risk framework is used
state: Learned patient state embedding from structured EHR and ClinicalBERT-derived text/context
observation_decoder: Patient model predicts next glycemic state/reward-related outcomes used for insulin-regimen optimization
action: Insulin regimen/dose recommendations across daily decision periods
action_provenance: Historical clinician-administered insulin for model learning; model recommendations reviewed and could be overridden by physicians in prospective use
transition_mechanism: Transformer-based patient dynamics model coupled with model-based reinforcement-learning policy
maximum_horizon: One-day model horizon with seven intra-day periods; prospective recommendations can be repeated for up to five days
rollout_regime: Recursive patient-model interaction for policy optimization, followed by physician-in-the-loop real deployment
capability_claim: Planning: RL policy selects insulin regimens through learned patient-model rollouts
baselines: Deep-learning predictors, standard clinical methods, and junior/intermediate physician recommendations; no clean action-agnostic patient model comparator
state_fidelity_metrics: Insulin-dose MAE, glucose prediction measures including PCC/AUROC and weighted interval score, blinded expert assessment, and glycemic outcomes
transition_metrics: One-day/seven-period patient-model evaluation and repeated real daily use; no multi-horizon degradation curve beyond the designed horizon
rollout_stability: No explicit long-horizon drift audit; prospective physician review bounds deployment
action_sensitivity: Insulin recommendations are compared with physicians/standard methods, but no action-shuffle/removal or randomized dose-perturbation study is reported
calibration_and_uncertainty: Predictive distributions and weighted interval score are reported; no reliability diagram, ECE, calibration slope/intercept, or coverage-by-horizon result identified
external_validation: Frozen external-hospital retrospective evaluation plus prospective deployment and a registered single-arm patient trial
decision_utility: Blinded physician comparisons, recommendation adoption/override workflow, prospective glycemic control, and trial endpoint
safety_evaluation: Hypoglycemia, severe hypoglycemia, severe hyperglycemia/ketosis, physician override, and prospective monitoring are explicitly reported; no severe episodes occurred in the 16-patient trial
statistical_analysis: Confidence intervals/significance tests are reported; trial primary endpoint decreased mean daily capillary glucose from 11.1 ± 3.6 to 8.6 ± 2.4 mmol/L (P<0.01)
causal_language: Uses optimized-control and proof-of-concept efficacy language, but the final clinical trial is small and single-arm
estimand: Trial pre-specified within-patient change in mean daily capillary blood glucose; model-development objective is optimized glycemic reward/regimen
confounding_strategy: Retrospective model training is observational; prospective trial uses before/after single-arm design without randomized control
positivity_and_overlap: No comprehensive treatment-support/overlap analysis for insulin-policy recommendations is reported
counterfactual_validation: External validation, blinded physician review, prospective deployment, and a registered single-arm feasibility trial; no randomized target-trial validation
code_access: Public RL-DITR code repository is reported
weights_access: Unclear: reusable trained weights were not confirmed
data_access: Minimum dataset is publicly deposited on Zenodo; fuller clinical data are governed/request-based
preprocessing_reproducibility: Public code and minimum dataset plus detailed methods support substantial reproduction; full EHR pipeline remains governed
randomness: Training/evaluation procedures are documented; exact seed/repeated-training protocol is only partially clear
evidence_anchors: Methods on data sources, seven-period patient model, model-based RL, internal/external evaluation, prospective deployment, and trial; main tables/figures for MAE, physician comparison, glycemic outcomes, and safety; Data/Code Availability; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05409391
appraisal_strengths: Large multicenter longitudinal dataset, patient-model rollouts, external validation, clinician comparison, prospective deployment, explicit override/safety monitoring, and registered real-patient trial
appraisal_limitations: Single-arm 16-patient trial, short horizon, no randomized clinical comparator, limited calibration evidence, unclear weights, and incomplete public data

title: Simulating the outcome of amyloid treatments in Alzheimer's disease from imaging and clinical data.
domain: Alzheimer's disease multimodal progression and hypothetical treatment simulation
dataset_or_cohort: Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) amyloid-positive longitudinal cohort
sample_scale: 442 participants with 2,781 visits/time points over 0-16 years; diagnostic groups reported as 71, 33, 131, 105, and 102 across study strata
institution_count: Multicenter ADNI observational study; institution count not treated as an independent external split
split_strategy: Internal model fitting/evaluation on ADNI with subgroup analyses; no held-out external cohort in this primary study
observation_process: Irregular longitudinal MRI, amyloid PET (AV45), FDG-PET, and seven clinical/cognitive scores; at least one complete multimodal visit required
missingness: Follow-up visits may lack modalities and are handled in the longitudinal model; entry requires at least one complete visit
censoring_or_competing_events: Longitudinal dropout is present but no explicit informative-censoring or competing-risk model is reported
state: Four latent disease components jointly governing imaging and clinical biomarker evolution
observation_decoder: Gaussian observation models decode latent disease state into multimodal imaging and clinical outcomes
action: Hypothetical amyloid lowering at 50% or 100%, varied by intervention time
action_provenance: Entirely simulated intervention applied to fitted disease dynamics; no treated patients are used for estimation
transition_mechanism: Coupled differential-equation disease-progression model with four latent processes and Gaussian decoders
maximum_horizon: Backward/forward disease-course simulation across approximately 20 years around conversion; observations span 0-16 years
rollout_regime: Free-running continuous-time simulation with natural-history and intervention branches
capability_claim: Counterfactual: compares unobserved disease trajectories under alternative amyloid-lowering dose and timing scenarios
baselines: Natural untreated trajectory, dose/time intervention scenarios, and model variants; no learned action-agnostic comparator distinct from natural history
state_fidelity_metrics: Fit to multimodal biomarker trajectories and clinical endpoints; agreement with known disease progression
transition_metrics: Trajectory-level simulated biomarker/clinical evolution and trial-compatible endpoint effects over intervention timing
rollout_stability: Long-range trajectories are plotted, but no explicit drift/constraint-violation metric or out-of-distribution stability audit
action_sensitivity: Explicit 50% versus 100% amyloid lowering and intervention-time sweeps against no-treatment natural history
calibration_and_uncertainty: Gaussian model uncertainty and simulated group variability are represented; no formal predictive calibration or interval-coverage validation is reported
external_validation: No frozen external cohort in the primary article; a supplementary independent-severity analysis is not treatment validation
decision_utility: Offline hypothetical trial design and intervention-timing insight; no clinician decision or prospective policy evaluation
safety_evaluation: No adverse-event, treatment-hazard, severity, override, or safety-constraint model
statistical_analysis: Simulation uncertainty and statistically powered endpoint calculations are reported; detailed inferential procedures are in methods/supplement
causal_language: Explicitly simulates hypothetical amyloid-treatment outcomes and interprets dose/timing differences as intervention effects, while acknowledging assumptions
estimand: Contrast in modeled clinical/biomarker trajectories under no treatment versus 50%/100% amyloid lowering at specified intervention times
confounding_strategy: No treatment-confounding adjustment because treated outcomes are absent; intervention effects are imposed through mechanistic assumptions
positivity_and_overlap: No empirical treatment positivity/overlap can be evaluated; simulated interventions may lie outside observed treatment support
counterfactual_validation: Compatibility with historical trial outcomes and biological plausibility only; no randomized treated-data validation
code_access: No public implementation identified for this article
data_access: ADNI data are credentialed and available through ADNI governance
preprocessing_reproducibility: Equations and cohort preprocessing are described, but absent code/parameters prevent end-to-end reproduction
randomness: Simulation sampling is described; exact software seeds and repeated fit protocol are not clearly reported
evidence_anchors: Methods on ADNI cohort, four-component disease model, Gaussian observation process, and intervention simulation; Results figures on 50%/100% lowering and intervention timing; Discussion explicitly states the hypothetical/model-assumption boundary
appraisal_strengths: Irregular multimodal trajectories, long free-running disease simulation, explicit no-treatment comparator, dose/timing perturbations, and clear mechanistic equations
appraisal_limitations: No treated data, no confounding/overlap identification, internal ADNI evidence only, no formal calibration, code, weights, or safety model; individual counterfactuals are model assumptions
source_status: Primary peer-reviewed full text inspected through PMC XML

title: Towards Causality-Aware Inferring: A Sequential Discriminative Approach for Medical Diagnosis.
publication_status: Peer-reviewed journal article (IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence, 2023)
domain: Sequential symptom inquiry and medical diagnosis
dataset_or_cohort: Muzhi (MZ) and Dxy (DX) medical dialogue datasets
sample_scale: MZ: 586 training and 142 test cases, 66 symptoms and 4 diseases; DX: 423 training and 104 test cases, 41 symptoms and 5 diseases
institution_count: Two distinct public/source datasets; clinical institution count not reported
split_strategy: Fixed train/test splits with five-fold tuning/analysis; out-of-distribution protocol trains on Ptrain and tests on broader Pall; five random seeds
observation_process: Sparse symptom-dialogue records; an agent sequentially asks up to a limited number of symptoms before diagnosis
missingness: Unrecorded symptoms are explicitly treated as missing; propensity latent matching estimates responses instead of assigning a biased default answer
censoring_or_competing_events: NA: short diagnostic dialogues with no time-to-event censoring or competing outcomes
state: Known, unknown, and inferred symptom state plus probabilistic disease belief
observation_decoder: Patient simulator returns symptom answers; diagnosis process returns disease probabilities/decision
action: Sequential symptom inquiry, with stopping/diagnosis decision
action_provenance: Simulated agent inquiries answered from passively collected dialogue records through a learned patient simulator
transition_mechanism: Propensity latent matching patient simulator plus progressive assurance agent with inquiry and intervention-inspired diagnostic processes
maximum_horizon: Reported inquiry budgets include 1 and 3 additional symptoms before diagnosis
rollout_regime: Closed-loop simulation: agent-selected inquiries update symptom/belief state and drive the next query or diagnosis
capability_claim: Planning: sequential agent selects symptom inquiries to increase diagnostic confidence and transportability
baselines: Prior medical diagnosis assistants/patient simulators, propensity-score matching variants, default-answer baselines, and model ablations
state_fidelity_metrics: Diagnostic success/accuracy and symptom-density/inquiry measures on MZ and DX, including out-of-distribution settings
transition_metrics: Performance after sequential inquiry budgets and under distribution shift; no long-horizon physiologic rollout
rollout_stability: Short fixed inquiry horizons reduce drift; no constraint-violation or extended stability audit
action_sensitivity: Known-symptom masking/intervention analyses and simulator matching ablations; no continuous dose/timing action perturbation
calibration_and_uncertainty: Probabilistic disease confidence and thresholds are used, but no reliability, ECE, calibration slope, or interval-coverage result is reported
external_validation: Cross-dataset evidence is reported separately, and OOD within-dataset testing is emphasized; not a frozen institutional clinical validation
decision_utility: Sequential diagnostic success and six-physician blinded comparison provide task utility
safety_evaluation: Limited inquiry budget and confidence-based diagnosis are safety-adjacent constraints; no explicit clinical harm severity, dangerous-misdiagnosis stress test, override, or monitoring plan
statistical_analysis: Five seeds and five-fold analyses are reported; comparative significance/variation is reported as in tables
causal_language: Uses causality-aware, intervention, and transportability language to remove inquiry/default-answer biases; it does not estimate a treatment effect
estimand: No explicit population causal estimand; target is transportable diagnosis under sequential symptom intervention/masking
confounding_strategy: Propensity latent matching adjusts selection in which symptoms were historically asked; residual unmeasured bias remains
positivity_and_overlap: Propensity matching addresses observed support indirectly; no full overlap diagnostics for every inquiry policy are reported
counterfactual_validation: OOD tests, masked-known-symptom analyses, and physician comparison; no randomized clinical diagnostic deployment
code_access: Public CAMAD implementation repository is reported
weights_access: Unclear: reusable trained checkpoints were not confirmed
data_access: MZ and DX benchmark data are public/available through cited sources and repository instructions
preprocessing_reproducibility: Public code and benchmark splits support substantial reproduction; some original data provenance/preprocessing remains dataset-dependent
randomness: Five random seeds are explicitly reported
evidence_anchors: Methods on propensity latent matching, progressive assurance agent, MZ/DX datasets, OOD Ptrain-to-Pall design, and inquiry budgets; Results/ablation tables; physician evaluation; official CAMAD repository
appraisal_strengths: Explicit missing-symptom bias problem, sequential closed-loop evaluation, OOD protocol, matching ablations, multiple datasets, physician comparison, code, and repeated seeds
appraisal_limitations: Small benchmark disease spaces, sparse retrospective dialogues, simulator-based rather than live-patient interaction, partial causal assumptions, no formal calibration or explicit harm testing
source_status: Primary full text inspected through the official arXiv manuscript corresponding to the TPAMI article; journal DOI and repository verified
